scope: Reviewed the Terraform under `infra/terraform` (24 folders), where most recent changes happen. The Grafana and Kubernetes folders were not reviewed.

scan.finding: VPC ID typed in tfvars files
Security groups mixing inline and separate rules

candidates.title: Create `modules/vm-host` and move the 6 hosts onto it
candidates.problem: 6 services repeat about 70 lines each: instance, Elastic IP, association, security group, and tags. The KMS key ARN is typed 7 times, and 2 hosts forgot `http_tokens = "required"`.
candidates.change: Create a `vm-host` base that owns those resources with the shared defaults, and move each host onto it with `moved` blocks so nothing is recreated.
gains: A new host is one 15-line module call instead of 70 lines in 3 files
The KMS key and metadata settings are set in 1 place instead of 6
The 2 hosts without required IMDSv2 tokens get it from the base default
Each plan shows only moves: 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy

before.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A[services/api] --> I1[aws_instance + eip + sg]
  W[services/worker] --> I2[aws_instance + eip + sg]
  R[services/registry] --> I3[aws_instance + eip + sg]
  K[KMS ARN typed 7x]
  I1 -.-> K
  I2 -.-> K
  I3 -.-> K
  classDef problem stroke:#c62828,stroke-width:2px
  class I1,I2,I3,K problem
before.caption: Three of the six hosts shown; each copies the same blocks.

after.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A[services/api] --> B[modules/vm-host]
  W[services/worker] --> B
  R[services/registry] --> B
  B --> K[data aws_kms_alias]
  classDef merged stroke:#16794a,stroke-width:3px
  class B merged
after.caption: Each host calls the base with its size and name.

candidates.verify: The plan of each of the 6 services shows only moved resources.
candidates.warning: The `worker` host uses `cpu_credits = "standard"` while the others use `unlimited`; decide in step 5 whether that is on purpose.

candidates.title: Look up the VPC and subnets by tag instead of typing their IDs in 11 tfvars files
candidates.problem: The VPC ID is typed in 11 files and the main subnet ID in 7. Recreating the VPC, or adding a second environment, means editing all of them.
candidates.change: Add a `lookups` helper that finds the VPC and subnets by their `Name` tag and outputs the IDs; services read it instead of a variable.
gains: The VPC ID lives in 0 files; the tag lives in 1 helper
A new service no longer copies network IDs into its tfvars
Plans show no changes, because the lookup returns the same IDs

  class L merged

candidates.title: Merge the 5 roots that each hold one `modules/proxy` call into one root with a `for_each` map
candidates.problem: 5 roots exist only to call `modules/proxy` once. Each has its own `versions.tf`, backend, and CI entry: 5 folders and 5 plans for 5 map entries.
candidates.change: Create one `services/publications` root with a map of publications, and move each one into it with `removed` blocks in the old roots and `import` blocks in the new one.
gains: A new publication is one map entry instead of a new folder with 3 files
Removes 4 copies of the provider and backend blocks

flowchart TB

  A[services/admin] --> P

  class D,A,S,B problem

after.mermaid:

  class U merged

candidates.verify: The old roots' plans show only removals from state, and the new root's plan shows only imports.

top.why: It changes nothing running, takes an hour, and makes the `vm-host` base simpler, because the base can use the lookup from the start.
